rationale: Round 4 plan (replaces round 2's 50 % gyroid, 6 copies). Stock 0.20mm QUALITY @MK3 + Prusament PETG (filament_type PETG = print_requirements; 250 °C, first layer 240, bed 90/85, fan 30-50 %: all inside 230-250 / 80-90 and the skill's PETG range, so not overridden). Overrides meet print_requirements.json exactly as strength rounds 3/4 modelled the bracket: 4 perimeters, 5 top / 5 bottom layers, 100 % rectilinear (solid: at 50 % gyroid the horn clamp falls to SF 2.91 in the drop; rectilinear because gyroid is not meant for 100 %), 0.2 mm layers. Elephant-foot 0.2 pairs with the 0.4 mm bed chamfer and keeps the bed-face horn pocket true. Copies 2 = spec §7: 6 brackets, 2 per plate, the same file printed on 3 plates, 6 h per plate (sliced 4.38 h). Orientation is in the STL (brief): hub plate on the bed, horn pocket on the bed face, vertical plate standing, window roof up. No library rows (materials.csv and lessons.md are empty), so no flow, temperature or xy compensation overrides. Seam: aligned (stated explicitly), which keeps seams in corners: random would scatter them over the window's faces (0.1 mm end clearance) and rear would put them on the flat +y tab face. Checked in the G-code: the posts' seams sit in the 90° corners where the window, notch, pilot and roof edges meet the +y (tab and gusset) face; the outline's at the arm's far corner (x 51, y -6.5); the floor band's in the ramp corner at x 1.9; the horn pocket's at the horn-arm tip. The governing sections (post roots, pilot row, band under the window) are loaded across the layers, where a seam does not cut the bonded area, so staggered inner seams are not needed here. Brim: none (brim_width 0): PETG barely warps, 1205 mm² of bed contact per bracket on a 60 x 30 mm footprint, and a brim would fill the 0.4 mm bed chamfer.
